campaign.title: Aurelia 1978 launch campaign and Logix Computer Academy
campaign.objective: Introduce Aurelia and its business software through press and television advertising, NCC presentations, a ComputerLand sales premiere and the public launch of Logix Computer Academy.
message: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
Learn before you decide.

Business Tools organise office work; Abacus supports planning; independently owned SSG General Ledger maintains accounting records. AION supplies tools and porting support while SSG owns and sells the application.
audience: Nontechnical business owners and managers; secondary audiences are dealers, software developers and peripheral manufacturers.

marketing_steps.description: Introduce Aurelia through newspaper and business-press teasers, then invite customers and press to the premiere.

marketing_presentation.description: Begin newspaper and business-press teasers on {start_date}, introducing Aurelia as a personal assistant in business. Start with “coming this spring”, then publish the {premiere_date} premiere date and invite brochure and presentation-invitation requests.

Follow the teasers with explanatory print advertisements about Aurelia, Abacus and independently branded SSG General Ledger. Prioritise markets with demonstration, support and Academy coverage, so readers can act on the campaign through local demonstrations and training enquiries.

During late May and early June, organise joint Logix/SSG press previews, prepare dealers and demonstration staff, issue launch invitations and rehearse the Aurelia presentation. Staff telephone enquiries, mailed brochures, demonstration appointments and Academy bookings.

marketing_steps.description: Run the cinematic Aurelia television commercial and direct viewers to demonstrations.

marketing_presentation.description: The proposed advertisement is a {duration_seconds}-second film trailer, with {lead} proposed as its lead. In the final {reveal_seconds} seconds, show Aurelia, Abacus, a printed result, the logo and the June 5 premiere date. Include a recognisable, independently branded SSG General Ledger report; explain accounting in the accompanying press campaign and follow-up films. Casting remains subject to contract.

Narrator introduces This spring. Douglas discusses a remarkably helpful new assistant during a therapy session. The reveal identifies Aurelia as a computer, and the therapist becomes curious about a demonstration. Warm humour, concrete business benefits and consistent interaction; avoid unhealthy dependency or claims of speech recognition/artificial intelligence. Telephone enquiries, mailed brochures, demo appointments and Academy bookings; trained staff handle responses.

marketing_steps.description: Introduce Aurelia as a business assistant at NCC on 5 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: Present on the {stage}, using {projector_count} video projectors. Record the full presentation and make it available to television broadcasters under {rebroadcast_terms}.
Open with the {computer} television commercial.

{presenter} describes {development_period} of work to bring {computer} to market. Early cars used tillers, levers, rotary cranks and cross-shaped handles before the steering wheel became the familiar standard. Personal computers reached an important milestone in {assembled_computer_year}: buyers no longer had to assemble them. Yet their controls still resemble those early experiments—awkward, inconsistent and hard to learn. He introduces Aurelia as a computer with a steering wheel: a consistent, intuitive way to work.

{presenter} reveals {computer_count} Aurelia computers. A camera circles them, showing every angle on the projection screens. Then show {commercial_count} new commercials: a housewife prints recipes, a schoolboy uses the on-screen calculator, and a businessman checks his diary of meetings and tasks.

{presenter} switches on {computer} and opens the {tools} menu. He loads a text document from disk, demonstrates editing, cursor navigation and selection, and copies and pastes text. He then finds a contact in the directory and pastes its details into the document, showing how familiar actions carry across applications.
{presenter} connects a printer while the computer remains on and prints the document. He demonstrates the calculator and a calendar of tasks and events, then prints the next day’s schedule.

{presenter} connects another disk drive and loads {spreadsheet} from disk. He explains its rules and calculations, then opens a large, complex accounting sheet. Changing one input immediately updates calculations throughout the sheet; he prints the result. He asks, “How many commands did I have to memorise?” to underline that the audience has followed familiar actions rather than memorised instructions.

{presenter} invites {os_speaker} from {os_company}, {logix_speaker} from {computer_company}, {software_speaker} from {software_company}, and a representative of {retailer} onto the stage. He introduces the {platform_bits}-bit platform, with its specifications displayed on the screens.

{speaker} explains that Aurelia runs applications for {compatible_version} and introduces {new_version} with a text user interface. The operating system belongs to {owner} and is available to other manufacturers whose hardware meets its requirements. He thanks {partner} for supporting this approach.
{speaker} presents Aurelia configurations and the {support_levels}-level support system, including telephone help through a call centre.

{speaker} introduces {ide} and announces a single joint tools and General Ledger presentation on {developer_session}. {software_company} and {application_company} have adapted the independently owned ledger to native C and the shared TUI; the morning session releases the port and demonstrates how it was built.
The {retailer} representative announces product availability in its shops from {retail_date}. {speaker} introduces {academy}, opening on {academy_date}, and the try-before-you-buy programme.

{presenter} explains {company}’s plans for expansion cards, FlexiBUS devices and monitors: limited further in-house development, with third-party products welcomed. Products meeting the compatibility criteria can receive {certification}. He invites everyone to try Aurelia at the booth.

Close with questions. Keep reminders on screen for the joint AION C IDE and SSG General Ledger launch ({developer_session}), ComputerLand sales premiere ({retail_date}) and Logix Academy launch ({academy_date}).

marketing_steps.description: Launch AION C IDE, the Software Developer Package and SSG General Ledger for Aurelia together on the morning of 6 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: Introduce the platform interfaces that the Software Developer Package exposes: FlexiBUS, display interfaces, implementation and licensing, compatibility and third-party peripheral development. Explain how those interfaces support application and peripheral work on Aurelia.

Use {ide} with {sdk} to edit a small application with syntax highlighting and diagnostic navigation. Build it using a qualified optimization profile, link an assembly library and debug the application in RAM. Explain C source portability and the need for separate target builds rather than promising universal binary compatibility.

Demonstrate keyboard-operated TUI forms with bounded data controls and calls into the shared ROM TUI. Show text and bitmap presentation in tested modes, distinguishing SDK composite helpers from native ROM services. Publish measured memory, disk and performance results; shared source and API contracts do not imply that future targets have already been released.

SSG demonstrates its General Ledger port within the same presentation: select a chart and department, enter and validate a balanced journal, correct an entry, review account balances and print a report. Show bounded forms, account tables, dropdown selection, Tab navigation, shortcuts and shared editing/copy-paste. This is a port of the separately released CBASIC product, not the launch of an accounting suite.

Compare the original CP/M/CBASIC release and native C/TUI port on the same Aurelia configuration with identical data and financial outputs. Identify runtime/build versions actually tested, compiler options, RAM, drives and cache conditions. Time validation, lookup, posting and report preparation separately from physical printing. Measure ROM TUI and assembly-library contributions; publish measured results only, with no promised multiplier or claim that language alone explains all responsiveness.

Export selected ledger balances and period totals through the documented disk file, close General Ledger, then open Abacus and reconcile imported control totals. SSG explains independent ownership, licensing, sales and specialist support. Finish the combined presentation with shared questions and record the full session under the agreed partner clearances.

marketing_steps.description: Hold the official Aurelia sales premiere at a ComputerLand shop on 14 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: {dealer} hosts the official Aurelia sales premiere with {logix}. Introduce the retail offering, demonstrate the business-assistant workflow and help visitors choose a suitable system and associated software. Keep separately licensed SSG General Ledger and training distinct from the computer purchase.

marketing_steps.description: Launch Logix Computer Academy and SSG General Ledger training on 16 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: The Academy was established on {established_date} and is announced publicly on {announcement_date}. Officially launch on {launch_date} with an initial {city_count}-city US programme with a {fundamentals_days}-day Fundamentals course. Small classes, substantial hands-on time, ideally one machine per participant or pair; business tools, introductory Abacus and advice on appropriate configurations and unnecessary purchases. Order and pay at training centres; immediate collection only where stock is available. No purchase obligation.

The {launch_date} Academy launch includes SSG-authorised General Ledger courses, direct distribution, dealer preparation and access to SSG specialist help. Teach chart setup, journal entry, corrections, reports, period-end work, backup/restore and reconciled Abacus summary export. Dealers handle installation, SSG handles application defects and accounting questions, and Logix handles hardware. Software licences, courses and setup services are separate offerings.

marketing_steps.description: Record the NCC presentations and distribute cleared television coverage.

marketing_presentation.description: Before NCC, contact television stations and arrange presenter, partner, music and production rights for redistribution. Include Michael Douglas commercial footage only if it is separately cleared for that use.

Throughout 5–8 June 1978, use a professional multi-camera crew to record every Logix NCC presentation and hands-on demonstration, including the premiere, technical and developer content, partner appearances, additional sessions and questions. Capture clean presenter audio, audience reactions and close-ups of the computer, display, connections and printouts. Retain full-session recordings and production masters.

Preserve demonstration fidelity: do not accelerate startup or recalculation, hide failures with misleading cuts or present recorded footage as a live result. Identify edited excerpts and any recorded fallback.

After NCC, prepare a business-user broadcast feature, short station-ready news and demonstration excerpts, clean captioned footage, separate narration or audio where practical, a factual product and Academy press sheet, and full edited presentations for longer technical coverage. Offer cleared, Logix-identified material to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix arranges normal duplication, dispatch and station-compatible copies. Distribution follows editing and clearance. Stations choose their own participation, schedules and editorial selection; no airtime or endorsement is guaranteed.

marketing_steps.description: Plan year-end workshops and customer-led expansion after the launch.

marketing_presentation.description: Prepare General Ledger year-end workshops and supported-edition update demonstrations. Keep customer data under customer control and obtain consent before using case studies or endorsements. This is follow-up planning, not a claim that year-end work is complete within the campaign period.

Expand demonstrations and qualified support using verified General Ledger customer results. Any SSG Model II or Apple II port requires a separate scope, build and qualification; the existing Tandy agreement covers Abacus only.

campaign.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign
campaign.objective: Demonstrate portable C applications and compatible peripherals and displays across computer brands, introduce the June 1979 Apple II/S-100 offerings, and recruit independent implementers through dated qualification and follow-up.
message: Choose your computer. Keep your investment.
Build on Aurelia, run native code on Apple II, and retain familiar interaction with Logix video.
Independent software, peripherals and displays can adopt shared standards without adopting the whole Logix platform.
audience: Business customers choosing computers, applications and peripherals.
Independent computer and peripheral manufacturers evaluating compatibility programmes.
Software publishers, developers, dealers and integrators supporting existing and future systems.

marketing_steps.description: Recruit independent computer, software and peripheral implementers.

marketing_presentation.description: Logix coordinates outreach, AION supports software and application integration, and DRI supports CP/M qualification. Prioritise North Star, with Lifeboat as a possible integration/distribution partner, then Vector Graphic. Both are strong CP/M prospects; FlexiBUS is a moderately strong fit, while Logix video is a moderate fit for North Star and a lower fit for Vector. Existing applications and display investment shape each proposal; outreach does not establish an agreement.

Cromemco is a moderate CP/M/FlexiBUS prospect but a weak Logix-video prospect because of its independent OS and graphics strategy. Altos is a moderately strong CP/M prospect with moderate FlexiBUS and limited video potential. Intertec has moderately strong CP/M and moderate host-specific FlexiBUS potential; schedule late-1979 evaluation and possible 1980 qualification. Heath/Heathkit is a moderate CP/M/FlexiBUS prospect for later feasibility work. Neither implies a June release or a host redesign.

Seek independent implementations in printers, disks, communications, input, instruments and specialist output. Match opportunities to vendor-owned product variants rather than relabelling every existing device. Printing needs explicit character/status and paper handling; plotting and specialist functions need their own profiles, while disks need geometry, durable writes, boot and recovery rules. Native faster disk interfaces remain valid.

marketing_steps.description: Publish separate compatibility profiles and update them for the June offerings.

marketing_presentation.description: Publish {cpm} host/CPU, memory and adapter requirements alongside DRI’s portable-extension release. Ordinary CP/M remains usable without TUI or FlexiBUS; extended services and application binaries require named supported configurations. Explain {tui} as shared interaction and {c} as source-level contracts with separate target builds. The Apple II/S-100 profiles and AION C 2.0 arrive at the June launch; later ERA and pointer capabilities are outside this release.

Publish {bus} electrical/transport rules, host drivers, device classes and diagnostics independently of CP/M and video. One device connects to each point-to-point port; passive hubs and daisy chains are unsupported, and the faster rate is at most {rate} KB/s before overhead. Distinguish the C display API, video controller and {video} monitor connection. Eighty columns require a qualified 640-pixel monitor; a consumer TV or existing 320-pixel monitor does not become compatible through a cable.

Provide {sdk}, published versions, reference-driver access, conformance tests, configuration diagnostics and a certification dispute process. State non-exclusive own-brand implementation and component-access principles, supply priorities and manufacturer participation. Settle reference-code rights, CP/M licensing, support duration/staffing, maintenance funding, governance, certification scope, allocations and warranties before firm offers. Preserve each supplier’s ownership, branding and specialist support.

marketing_steps.description: Qualify the demonstrations, supplier contributions and public disclosure.

marketing_presentation.description: Rehearse named configurations with supplier workshops and record failures and corrections. Test the Aurelia/Model II document round trip separately from Aurelia compilation, FlexiDisk II Apple-format writing and Apple II execution. Measure memory/workspace, disk formats, loading/recalculation, UI redraw and peripheral behaviour; test ROM-bank restoration across display/disk calls. Book suitable space and audiovisual equipment, secure participant clearance and label prepared data or recordings.

Keep the Model II demonstration labelled prototype until its release. AION supplies the June cards; SMC is a future source subject to chip qualification. Apple’s participation concerns native Apple products, not S-100 endorsement. Separate shipping products, qualified demonstrations, prototypes and recruitment prospects; manufacturer interest, forecasts and targets are not sales or commitments.

Until {reveal}, describe the new architecture only as next-generation computers. Withhold product/processor/OS names, word size, ISA/registers, memory organization, clocks, performance figures, chip counts, schematics, board images, bus topology, future displays and coprocessor internals. Apply this to talks, Q&A, press, dealers, OEMs and attachments. Current CP/M/FlexiBUS/video documentation and the released Apple 6502 target are public. Answer architecture questions with the NCC 1980 disclosure plan; make no unspecified support-duration, withdrawal or engineering guarantee.

marketing_steps.description: Present cross-platform C development, familiar interfaces and the independent ecosystem.

marketing_presentation.description: The presentation lasts {programme_minutes} minutes, followed by questions. Show current products first and label the supplier roadmap separately.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Open with independent choice: shared application interfaces, documents and peripherals let customers keep useful work while changing computer brands. Introduce the software, bus and display standards as independently adoptable.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. DRI explains the portable CP/M extensions. Demonstrate an Abacus document round trip between Aurelia and the {model} prototype using separately qualified editions and an explicit transfer path. Show the {option} as a prototype; its recorded release is {release}, not the NCC date.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Feature {ledger} as an independent C-application pioneer. SSG demonstrates its native Z80 AION C implementation, ROM TUI forms and versioned balance exports to Abacus, explaining the benefit of shared editing and controls while retaining its accounting rules, ownership and support. This is General Ledger, not a larger accounting suite, a Model II port or a newly released Apple edition. Show how {basic} also uses shared TUI services without describing BASIC as a C port.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Operate a qualified FlexiBUS peripheral sequentially on named hosts. Show identification, supported class functions and driver requirements, attaching only with the port quiescent. Introduce the Apple II Expansion Card, S-100 FlexiBUS Interface and dual-format FlexiDisk II as separate choices.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Present {apple_video} and {s100_video} with ROM-backed TUI and callable libraries. On matching qualified monitors, demonstrate the full June 1979 Aurelia control behaviour and text/bitmap/sprite modes: frames, windows, editing, selection and redraw. Apple uses native 6502 code; S-100 TUI requires qualified CP/M/TUI extensions. Explain keyboard-command mappings and independent host performance. Preserve native Apple graphics/sound access; no automatic conversion of legacy graphics or later mouse/professional modes is implied.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Launch {compiler}: edit and compile a small shared C sample on Aurelia, save the native 6502 executable on an Apple DOS 3.2-compatible disk using {disk}, move the disk to Apple II and run it under its existing DOS installation. A compatible Disk II reader needs no Logix interface merely to read the disk; directly connecting FlexiDisk II to Apple does. Rebuild common TUI/drawing calls for Logix video, then show separately named native Apple graphics and speaker functions. The IDE stays on Aurelia; CPU-specific assembly and direct hardware access still need adapters. An Apple representative joins this native Apple demonstration without endorsing S-100 systems.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Give independent hardware pioneers a dedicated roadmap segment. Use {bridge} and {printer} to explain vendor-owned FlexiBUS bridge/native-interface approaches, and {leedex} and {sanyo} to explain purpose-built digital-input monitor variants. These are candidate paths in June, not shipping products or confirmed stage participants: the recorded estimated releases are {bridge_date}, {printer_date}, {leedex_date} and {sanyo_date}, respectively. Native Centronics printers remain behind a bridge; existing composite monitors do not become digital through a cable. Describe only tested raster/readability profiles, without promising 80 columns on every monitor. Invite supplier representatives only once participation and claims are cleared.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. {presenter} explains that shared C logic and documented APIs reduce migration work, while target-specific builds, data-format validation and testing remain necessary. Future computers will not execute Z80 binaries natively; describe the planned optional Z80 compatibility path without revealing its implementation. Continue CP/M tools and maintenance alongside future development; eight-bit systems retain business, home and education roles without a fixed replacement date.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Close with available products, prototype demonstrations and prospective supplier programmes clearly distinguished. Direct customers to dealer demonstrations and developers to the SDK, compatibility directory, migration clinics and implementation programme.

marketing_steps.description: Run dealer demonstrations, trade-press activity and developer clinics.

marketing_presentation.description: Reuse the NCC demonstrations and compatibility guides rather than repeat the keynote. Teach C target adapters, console/file portability, the Apple disk-transfer workflow, ROM TUI bindings and device-class drivers. Publish named supported configurations, application editions, test failures and support contacts; distinguish shipping products, prototypes and qualification work.

Refresh the pioneer directory as products become available. The Model II CP/M/FlexiBUS release is {tandy_date}; the {bridge} has an estimated {bridge_date} release. Later printer and monitor candidates stay on the roadmap until their own dates and qualification evidence. Suppliers retain their own brands, licences, sales and support.

marketing_steps.description: Review adoption targets and the evidence behind ecosystem growth.

marketing_presentation.description: By end-1979, target Tandy shipping, one additional OEM selling a supported CP/M-extension or FlexiBUS configuration, another in qualification and verified devices in several categories. By NCC 1980, target {manufacturers} distinct non-Logix manufacturers. Count Tandy once; exclude duplicate dealer builds and SKUs. These are goals, not achieved totals.

Track compatible-computer sell-through, qualified C and other application editions, peripheral shipments/classes, document interchange, support incidents, supplier concentration and component availability. Compare each pioneer’s actual scope and release date with the directory; separate application use of an API, bus implementation and digital-monitor compatibility. Do not turn adoption assumptions into measured sales.

marketing_steps.description: Publish customer evidence and prepare the next campaign.

marketing_presentation.description: Assemble verified customer examples, compatibility results and supplier configurations. Report progress and unresolved access/support issues, keeping future releases and NCC 1980 targets separate from results. The {printer} is recorded only to {release_month}; do not infer shipment by this January review from month precision alone. Leedex and Sanyo digital variants remain later roadmap items. Maintain the architecture embargo until the announced reveal.

campaign.title: Artemis. A new generation. A familiar way to work.
campaign.objective: Communicate the launch, qualify demonstrations and coordinate follow-up described by the source campaign.

marketing_steps.description: Introduce Artemis, demonstrate its workflows and explain the compatibility commitment.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. {presenter}: the business task and familiar way to work
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. AIONix multitasking: edit, calculate and switch using familiar TUI conventions

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Native Business Tools and Abacus 2 charts/document fields; then SSG demonstrates General Ledger on its qualified CP/M legacy path; a native ERA port remains a separately qualified later edition
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. One maintained C project, separate ERA and Z80 builds; optional compatibility card runs qualified unchanged legacy binaries
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Aurelia+, PDP-11/34 and Artemis: verified calculation benchmark, then visible animation
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Reveal: 32-bit RISC ERA 1 developed by AION

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Publish the compatibility commitment through 2000 and its precise scope Announce the compatibility commitment on {announcement_date}, with support through {support_end}. This is a commitment; future fulfilment remains to be demonstrated. Released Artemis application binaries using documented, supported ERA/AIONix interfaces retain a supported execution path on subsequent Logix professional platforms through 2000: native execution, a maintained compatibility runtime, or emulation. Source portability is a separate commitment, not a substitute for the binary execution path. Undocumented hardware access, unqualified peripherals and unsupported interfaces; no promise of unchanged speed, unlimited memory, or every future device. Z80 programs use their separately qualified compatibility path. Publish versioned ABI/API eligibility and conformance tests; preserve reference binaries and regression workloads; budget compatibility engineering, runtime distribution and support. Staffing, funding and validation remain explicit launch readiness gates.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Partners: independent SSG head, Digital Research and qualified device/software partners
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Qualified configurations, order routes, developer kits and training
After the 55-minute presentation

Incremental qualified 80×40 and 80×25 high-resolution text demonstrations, grayscale bitmap/sprites, explicit old-monitor limitations and replaceable card. Retain existing presentation duration; incorporate into Artemis product demonstration.
The independent native business application presented is {subject}; its qualification and support remain separate.

marketing_steps.description: Compare computation and display workloads under reproducible conditions.

marketing_presentation.description: Compare {systems}, using separately measured computation and rendering paths.

Identical vector transformations and fixed-point precision, inputs, rounding and verified output; time computation separately from rendering and I/O. Publish source, compiler options, configuration and repeat-run range.
Same shaded rotating cube, geometry and image quality; identify display hardware, frame-buffer and display-transfer costs separately. Do not infer pure CPU speed from unequal graphics systems.
Publish measured ratios only after reproducible qualification; no forecast assumes an unmeasured speed multiplier.

marketing_steps.description: Qualify application, licensing, resource and support claims before publication.

marketing_presentation.description: Beyond the 64 KB application barrier; demonstrate a measured resident workload on a named 128 KB or 256 KB configuration. Finite RAM and process limits remain; no demand paging promised.

Professional multitasking AIONix with Unix V7-inspired behaviour and familiar Logix TUI/keyboard conventions. Do not claim a Unix source licence or trademark endorsement without an established agreement.

Artemis-hosted AION C IDE supplies ERA native and Z80 cross-compilers, target libraries and separate executables. Portable code following guidelines can require small changes; quantify changes for each demonstration rather than promising zero work.

Native Abacus 2 and Business Tools; SSG General Ledger uses its qualified CP/M legacy path at this presentation. The separate native ERA edition is not claimed released here. Pulse 1 remains Aurelia+ software; a card demonstration requires guest OS/memory qualification. Native Pulse 3 and Abacus 3 launch only at COMDEX on November 19.
Aurelia+ remains a supported value option; compatible independent 8-bit computers grow the ecosystem. No forced migration or promise that cheaper 8-bit demand disappears.
Measured benchmark and reproducible display comparison
Qualified demo memory/process footprint and printing paths
Published native/card application matrix and OS licensing status
Versioned compatibility policy, engineering owner, staffing and funded maintenance plan
Dealer stock/service readiness and Academy instructor qualification

campaign.title: COMDEX 1979 campaign and presentation
campaign.objective: Communicate the launch, qualify demonstrations and coordinate follow-up described by the source campaign.
message: More room to work. More freedom to choose.
Your existing software. Less waiting.
Calculate once. Chart it. Print the documents.

marketing_steps.description: Present Aurelia+, Abacus 2 and qualified partner applications at COMDEX 1979.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {programme_minutes} minutes for the presentation programme; questions and follow-up are separate.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. {presenter}: growing businesses need more capacity, less waiting and compatible choices.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Identical live calculated shaded-cube animation on Aurelia and Aurelia+, followed by identical Abacus recalculation and chart generation; present measured results. Use {explanation_minutes} minute for explanation and {animation_minutes} minutes for the live shaded cube. Calculate rotation, project vertices, determine visible faces, calculate shading and draw a fixed sequence of cube rotations live. No prerecorded animation or precomputed frames. Same executable and inputs on both machines, compatible with both Same resolution, shading method, rendering settings and equivalent qualified display configurations; disclose unavoidable differences Visible start countdown, elapsed time and completed-frame count Fixed frame/rotation sequence completes the same amount of work; no silent frame skipping or quality reduction Use a workload that fits both machines; demonstrate additional capacity separately Both machines must finish correctly; publish results only after measurement Same Abacus 2.0 executable, worksheet values/formulas, calculation settings and chart workload. Compare recalculation and chart-generation time; exclude physical printer time. Animation measures the combined calculation/display path, not pure CPU performance. The catalog clocks are 4 and 6 MHz, but no 1.5x or other application speedup is promised.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Chart employee pay values; link fields to a payslip layout; preview employees and print the entire batch. Demonstrate charts and document layouts populated by spreadsheet field values. Use the catalogued text-mode vertical or horizontal bar charts; do not imply unimplemented graphical chart types. Fictitious employees with names, departments, pay components, deductions and precalculated net pay; one row per employee. Inspect precalculated values and reconcile totals Show a payroll-cost bar chart by department Open one reusable payslip layout and identify linked spreadsheet fields Preview different employees to show field substitution Print one complete payslip per employee from the same layout Validate field mapping, missing values, numeric formatting and rounding Validate pagination and ensure every selected employee prints exactly once with the correct values Validate save/reopen and preserve spreadsheet/document contents Reconcile the separately demonstrated SSG General Ledger balances through versioned disk-file exchange; the fictitious employee values in this layout demonstration are not an SSG payroll export Abacus charts, formats and prints supplied calculations. Payroll law/rules, statutory deductions and updates belong to the payroll application or properly maintained worksheet. No direct ledger write-back or live database link. Supporting implementation advantage for useful workloads, not a permanently exclusive general technique. Promote Abacus 2.0 on both Aurelia and Aurelia+ in supported configurations. Do not imply a new computer is required.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. An SSG representative demonstrates General Ledger balances, period reports and a separate reconciled export to Abacus. No SSG payroll module or payroll calculation is presented.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Demonstrate a focused information-management task using tested, implemented capabilities; no implied live cross-application integration.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Introduce the Compatibility Kit, reference adapters and diagnostics. Show an independent application implementation only after qualification; otherwise show clearly labelled engineering work.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. SSG leadership joins participating peripheral/computer suppliers. Name products and distinguish shipping, qualified and prototype status.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Purchasing, existing-Aurelia upgrades, ongoing support and independent manufacturer participation; new hardware focus on Aurelia+.
The independent business application presented is {subject}; retain its own branding, licensing and support.

marketing_steps.description: Keep independent supplier roles and qualified configurations explicit.

marketing_presentation.description: Independent branding, management, licences and support. The head of SSG speaks immediately after Abacus and joins the partner segment.
Demonstrate only individually qualified configurations. Invitations and targets are not agreements or shipments.

Published interfaces and kit permit independent Aurelia-class implementations; support and certification optional. Native hardware adapters are valid; FlexiBUS and Logix video are separate profiles. Proper application/OS/firmware licences remain necessary.

marketing_steps.description: Explain upgrades, continued support and independent manufacturer participation.

marketing_presentation.description: Clearly identify the hardware, required software and printing configuration; distinguish SSG licences and specialist setup.
New capabilities for the computer you already own. Publish configuration requirements and explain workloads that benefit from Aurelia+.
Published specifications/self-tests, physical compatibility kits, optional bounded assistance and configuration-specific certification; no exclusive partnership required.
Interoperability sessions and verified directory listings; document production supplies a concrete printer use case.
Promote training, demonstration access and implementation help.
Logix focuses new hardware development and promotion on Aurelia+ while enabling independent Aurelia-class clones and maintaining installed-base support; no immediate withdrawal date.

marketing_steps.description: Explain migration without disclosing the future architecture early.

marketing_presentation.description: Full architecture disclosure is scheduled for {reveal_date}.
Native binary compatibility will change; established C practices reduce migration work; a planned optional Z80 path supports qualified legacy code.
No future product/processor/OS names, word size, architecture, future-target compiler output, binaries or revealing demonstrations before NCC 1980.

campaign.title: A clear view of your next design.
campaign.objective: Generate qualified CAD evaluations and dealer demonstrations for the Artemis/AutoCAD offering, showing a complete workflow from drawing entry to plotted output.
message: A clear view of your next design.
Autodesk AutoCAD on Logix Artemis PRO. From drawing to plotted output.
See the drawing clearly
Native 800x600 drawing area on the 17-inch screen, four shades selected from 16 levels, static CAD palette and demonstrated line quality.
Keep commands and drawing in view
Colour command/status display alongside the dedicated drawing screen, with explicit keyboard/mouse focus.
Take the drawing beyond the screen
Save, reopen, exchange and plot the same test drawing; verify coordinates and output scale.
Buy an application with a supported platform
Autodesk application support and Logix hardware/integration support, qualified configurations, dealer training and a clear upgrade route.
Bring a drawing. See it on Artemis. Take home the plot.
audience: primary_audiences / 0: Small engineering and architectural practices evaluating desktop CAD
primary_audiences / 1: Drafting departments and technical consultants
primary_audiences / 2: Specialist computer dealers and CAD resellers
secondary_audiences / 0: Independent software houses considering Artemis
secondary_audiences / 1: Existing Artemis owners evaluating a professional upgrade
